title: Why did the test result flip?
hook: Allocation changes across periods. Compare pooled and common-weight results.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: changing an A/B split partway through can reverse the pooled result.

misconception: Treating traffic shift mid-test as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: changing an A/B split partway through can reverse the pooled result.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Early A converts 90/100 and B 19/20; late A converts 2/20 and B 20/100. With equal weight on the two periods, which version wins?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-traffic-shift-mid-test/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Early period A90/100,B19/20; late period A2/20,B20/100. B beats A in each period (95>90%,20>10%) but A pooled92/120=76.6667% vs B39/120=32.5%. Standardize equal period weights A50%,B57.5%.

src/demos/probability/p100-traffic-shift-mid-test/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Early period A90/100,B19/20; late period A2/20,B20/100. B beats A in each period (95>90%,20>10%) but A pooled92/120=76.6667% vs B39/120=32.5%. Standardize equal period weights A50%,B57.5%.

claims.text: Equal-period weighting retains A=50%, B=57.5%. Pooling instead retains A=76.667%, B=32.5%, because A receives more early traffic and B more late traffic.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-traffic-shift-mid-test/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Early period A90/100,B19/20; late period A2/20,B20/100. B beats A in each period (95>90%,20>10%) but A pooled92/120=76.6667% vs B39/120=32.5%. Standardize equal period weights A50%,B57.5%.

claims.text: B is better in both periods. Changing assignment shares across time mixes treatment with period composition. A common weighting answers the stated equal-period question; it does not automatically repair every adaptive experiment.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-traffic-shift-mid-test/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Early period A90/100,B19/20; late period A2/20,B20/100. B beats A in each period (95>90%,20>10%) but A pooled92/120=76.6667% vs B39/120=32.5%. Standardize equal period weights A50%,B57.5%.

claims.text: One version receives mostly high-conversion Monday traffic, another mostly low-conversion Sunday traffic. What should you check first? Compare like periods or use a specified common weighting before interpreting a pooled difference.
